evidence: src/products/infrastructure/repositories/product.repository.ts: class ProductRepository keeps a private Map<string, Product> as its in-memory persistence store
save(product) only calls this.products.set(product.id.getValue(), product), which stores the product with no business logic
findById, findAll, delete and exists are simple Map lookups, removals and existence checks, all persistence work
The @Injectable() decorator is framework wiring, which fits the infrastructure layer
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file sits in the infrastructure layer, and everything it does is persistence work. ProductRepository is an in-memory store keyed by product id. It only offers save, findById, findAll, delete and exists, which are plain CRUD and lookup operations on a Map. It holds no business rules, no validation and no domain invariants. It also has no transport logic or use-case orchestration. The @Injectable decorator is NestJS framework wiring, which belongs in infrastructure. Its responsibilities match its declared layer.
